newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian Clutch Auto ties up with UK firm.
newsitem.headline: Indian Clutch Auto ties up with UK firm.

text.p: Indian clutch maker, Clutch Auto Ltd, has established a technical collaboration with Britain's Automotive Products Ltd, a senior company official said on Wednesday.

"The tie-up will start as a technical agreement, with scope for expansion into a financial joint venture. The onus is on us to translate their technology and ask for more," said V.K. Mehta, vice-chairman and managing director, Clutch Auto Ltd, while talking to journalists in the capital..

Earlier on Wednesday, the firm announced its results for 1996/97 (April to March). Its net profit fell to 21.52 million rupees in 1996/97 from 22.7 million in the previous year. Sales grew to 598.8 million rupees in 1996/97 from 461.5 million rupees in 1995/96..

Mehta said that the company was on course to achieve sales of 850 million rupees in 1997/98, and 2.0 billion rupees three years down the road in 1999/2000. He also expected margins to double in 1997/98..

"The company has been chosen as one of the three suppliers for (India's largest car maker) Maruti Udyog Ltd. It has alloted land to us for a plant at its new township outside Delhi, to make friction material for clutches and brakes," Mehta said..

He added that investment in the new facility would be $5.0 million, most of which was already in the pipeline. "Our endeavour is to increase exports to 30 percent of our production from the present 18 per cent," Mehta said..
A company statement said that Clutch Auto makes one million clutch discs and 0.5 million cover assemblies every year, and is the sole supplier to the defence industry..
